# Function to save numeric sequential copies of graphs in a path

auto_filename <- function(base, ext) {
  # Remove extension if accidentally included
  base <- sub(paste0("\\.", ext, "$"), "", base)
  full_path <- paste0(base, ".", ext)
  
  i <- 1
  while (file.exists(full_path)) {
    full_path <- paste0(base, "_", i, ".", ext)
    i <- i + 1
  }
  return(full_path)
}

# Introduction

First we filter and normalize the date, then we will do exploratory heatmaps and boxplots of the communities at different taxonomic levels

Load the Phyloseq object. The Phyloseq object doesn't let you just save its components as data.frames. So you need to use phyloseqCompanion for this. We can then create a stacked matrix of ASVs and metadata.

# Phyloseq load

Loading the phyloseq objects and filtering variables that we are not interested

```{r stacked dataframes, echo=FALSE}
phylo.reefs <- readRDS("data/bcm_reefs_raja2023.rds")
```

Note: For finished publisheable code, just upload final and filtered phyloseq

# ASVs filtering

**Data filtering**: Performing a low-count filter with ASVs having only appear 1 time (count), and 10% prevalence across samples.\ 

Note: This will filtering very rare taxa

```{r}
#Define filtering criteria
min_count <- 1
prev_threshold <- 0.10

#Get ASV/OTU table and sample count

asv_table <- otu_table(phylo.reefs) %>% 
  as.data.frame()
sample_count <- nsamples(phylo.reefs)

# Compute prevalence (proportion of samples where each ASV/OTU meets min_count)
prev_filter <- apply(asv_table, 1, function(x) sum(x >= min_count) / sample_count)

# Keep taxa that meet the prevalence threshold
phylo.reefs_filtered <- prune_taxa(prev_filter >= prev_threshold, phylo.reefs)

remove(min_count)
remove(prev_threshold)

#Save filtered phyloseq object for other markdowns and analysis (e.g., gllvm)
saveRDS(phylo.reefs_filtered, "data/bcms_filtered_raja2023.rds")
```

# Taxonomy table

```{r}
#taxonomy table
tax_table <- as.data.frame(phylo.reefs_filtered@tax_table) %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "ASV") %>% 
  mutate(Kingdom = as.factor(Kingdom), Phylum = as.factor(Phylum),
         Class = as.factor(Class), Order = as.factor(Order),
         Family = as.factor(Family), Genus = as.factor(Genus), 
         Species = as.factor(Species))

#ASV table
asv_table <- as.data.frame(phylo.reefs_filtered@otu_table) %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "ASV")

#combine taxonomy and OTU tables by ASV
reef.combined <- right_join(tax_table, otu_table, by = "ASV")
```

# TSS scaling

Performing a Total Sum Scaling (TSS) 

More info: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41522-020-00160-w


```{r}
tss_transform <- function(physeq_obj) {
  otu_table(physeq_obj) <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_obj, function(x) x / sum(x))
  return(physeq_obj)
}

phylo_tss <- tss_transform(phylo.reefs_filtered)
saveRDS(phylo_tss, "data/bcms_filtered&tss_reefs_raja2023.rds")
```

# Stacked dataframe

For further heatmap, boxplots, and PERMANOVA analysis we prepared a stacked dataframe (taxa_stacked)

Note: TAXA_INFO = ASV_TABLE

## Stacked all
```{r}
# Extract ASV table: from TSS phyloseq

asv_table_tss <- as.data.frame(phylo_tss@otu_table)

env <- sample.data.frame(phylo_tss@sam_data) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(site), all_vars(!is.na(.)))

# Pivot table into a stacked dataframe:
taxa_info_all <- cbind(asv_table_tss, phylo_tss@tax_table) %>% as.data.frame()
taxa_info_all$OTU <- rownames(taxa_info_all)
taxa_stacked <- pivot_longer(taxa_info_all, cols = phylo_tss@sam_data$sample_id,
                             values_to = "relative_abundance",
                             names_to = "sample_id") %>% as.data.frame()

if(any(table(taxa_stacked$sample_id) != nrow(phylo_tss@otu_table))) {
  message("STOP! Something went wrong stacking, not all sequences present for
          at least one of the samples")
}

# Adding meta-data to the stacked table
colnames(taxa_stacked)[9] <- "sample_id" #in this matrix was as Sample instead of sample_id

taxa_stacked <- left_join(taxa_stacked, env, by = "sample_id") %>% 
  filter_at(vars(site),all_vars(!is.na(.)))

gc()
write.csv(taxa_info_all, file="data/ASV_taxa_table_tss.csv")
write.csv(taxa_stacked, file="data/ASV_taxa_stacked_tss.csv")

```

## Top 10 Phyla barplot

Prepare dataframe
```{r}
#Get top 10 most abundant phyla (overall)
top_phyla <- taxa_stacked %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_abundance)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(Phylum)

#Collapse other phyla into "Other Phyla"
taxa_stacked_mod <- taxa_stacked %>%
  mutate(Phylum = ifelse(Phylum %in% top_phyla, Phylum, "Other Phyla"))

#Calculate percentage abundance per site_type and phylum
phylum_percentages <- taxa_stacked_mod %>%
  group_by(site_type, site, Phylum) %>%  #adjust categories you want to estimate percentages on
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(site) %>% #adjust to your target grouping visualization
  mutate(percentage = 100 * total_abundance / sum(total_abundance)) %>%
  ungroup()

#Determine stacking order by total abundance (ascending so most abundant is bottom)
phylum_order <- c(
  "Cyanobacteriota",
  "Proteobacteria",
  "Bacteroidota",
  "Planctomycetota",
  "Crenarchaeota",
  "Verrucomicrobiota",
  "Actinobacteriota",
  "Acidobacteriota",
  "Fusobacteriota",
  "Desulfobacterota",
  "Myxococcota",
  "Other Phyla"
)

#Set factor levels for Phylum to control stacking order
phylum_percentages$Phylum <- factor(phylum_percentages$Phylum, levels = phylum_order)

# Define colors for "Other Phyla"
all_colors <- phylum_colors2
all_colors["Other Phyla"] <- "grey70"

#Order sites
phylum_percentages$site <- factor(phylum_percentages$site,                                           
                       levels = order_sitetype)

```

Plot
```{r}
#Plot stacked barplot
phyla_stack_plot <- 
  ggplot(phylum_percentages, aes(x = site, y = percentage, fill = Phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = all_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Abundant Phyla by Site Type",
    x = "Site Type",
    y = "Relative Abundance (%)"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~site_type, scales = "free_x", labeller = labeller(site_type = facet_labels))
phyla_stack_plot
```

Save plot

```{r}
safe_filename <- auto_filename("figures/barplots/stacked_top10_phyla", "svg")  #adjust path and output file name
ggsave("figures/barplots/stacked_top10_phyla.svg", 
       plot = phyla_stack_plot, 
       device = "svg",
       width = 11,

```

# Heatmap 

Adjust the taxonomic value you want to plot

```{r Top 50}
fill = "Phylum"
taxa = "Genus"
topN = 50
all = FALSE
unidentified = FALSE
```

## Temporary df

```{r temporary dataframe}
# Setting up the temporary dataframe:
toplot <- taxa_stacked 
colnumber <- which(colnames(toplot) == fill)
colnumber2 <- which(colnames(toplot) == taxa)
colnames(toplot)[colnumber] <- "fill"
colnames(toplot)[colnumber2] <- "taxa"

# This replaces anything that has "Unknown" in the chosen fill and taxa groups with "Unidentified"
toplot[which(is.na(toplot$taxa)), "taxa"] <- "Unidentified"
toplot[which(grepl("Unknown", toplot$taxa)), "taxa"] <- "Unidentified"
toplot[which(toplot$taxa == "Unidentified"), 
       "fill"] <- paste0("Unidentified ", taxa)

# Creates a table with the taxonomies present after filtering 
taxonomic <- unique(toplot[, c("taxa", "fill")])
taxonomic$taxa <- as.factor(taxonomic$taxa)
taxonomic$fill <- as.factor(taxonomic$fill)

# The columns that you want to use for plotting need to be in the groups here:
toplot <- toplot %>%
  group_by(sample_id, area, site, taxa, fill, site_type,benthic_dom,connection, temperature,chla, conductivity,salinity, mat_color,mat_thickness,direct_substrate, substrate_group, biotic_abiotic, neigh1, neigh2) %>%  
   mutate(relative_abundance = as.numeric(relative_abundance)) %>% # Edit here from your metadata
  dplyr::summarise(relative_abundance = sum(relative_abundance)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Gets the MEAN COMMUNITY: 
toplot <- toplot %>%
  group_by(area, site, taxa, fill, site_type,benthic_dom,connection, temperature, conductivity,salinity, chla, mat_color,substrate_group) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(relative_abundance = mean(relative_abundance)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Orders the taxa by top abundance:
top <- toplot %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(taxa) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(meanAbun = mean(relative_abundance)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Top abundance of the "fill" group:
top2 <- toplot %>%
  group_by(area, site, fill, site_type,benthic_dom,connection, temperature, mat_color,
           conductivity,salinity, chla, substrate_group) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(relative_abundance = sum(relative_abundance)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  as.data.frame()
top2 <- top2 %>% 
  group_by(fill) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(meanAbun = mean(relative_abundance)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

toplot <- toplot[,-which(colnames(toplot) == "fill")]

if(all){topN = length(unique(toplot$taxa))}

top2 <- top2[order(top2$meanAbun, decreasing = TRUE), ]
top <- top[order(top$meanAbun, decreasing = TRUE), ]
selected <- top$taxa[1:topN]
toplot <- toplot %>% filter(taxa %in% selected)

taxonomic <- taxonomic[which(taxonomic[, "taxa"] %in% selected), ]

taxonomic <- left_join(taxonomic, top, by = "taxa")
colnames(taxonomic)[3] <- "taxaMeanAbun"
taxonomic <- left_join(taxonomic, top2, by = "fill")
colnames(taxonomic)[4] <- "fillMeanAbun"
taxonomic <- taxonomic[order(taxonomic$fillMeanAbun),]

toplot <- left_join(toplot, taxonomic, by = "taxa")

toplot[, "taxa"] <- factor(toplot[, "taxa"],
                           levels = taxonomic[, "taxa"])

multi.mixedorder <- function(..., na.last = TRUE, decreasing = TRUE){
  do.call(order, c(
    lapply(list(...), function(l){
      if(is.character(l)){
        factor(l, levels=gtools::mixedsort(unique(l)))
      } else {
        factor(as.character(l), levels=gtools::mixedsort(levels(l)))
      }
    }),
    list(na.last = na.last, decreasing = decreasing)
  ))
}

colnames(toplot)[which(colnames(toplot) == taxa)] <- "taxa"
colnames(toplot)[which(colnames(toplot) == fill)] <- "fill"

toplot$fill <- factor(toplot$fill, levels = rev(unique(taxonomic$fill)))

```

## Heatmap plot

Heatmap of the top 50 most abundant

```{r heatmap plot, echo=FALSE}
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Cyanobacteriota"           = "#b02b25",
  "Proteobacteria"            = "#185563",
  "Bacteroidota"              = "#00A087", 
  "Planctomycetota"           = "#3C5488",
  "Verrucomicrobiota"         = "#F39B7F",
  "Crenarchaeota"             = "#FFC857",
  "Acidobacteriota"           = "#9071C1",
  "Actinobacteriota"          = "#F26419",
  "Fusobacteriota"            = "#7E6148",
  "Unidentified"              = "darkgrey"
)


x <- 4  # nth root for alpha in heatmap

toplot2 <- toplot %>% 
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = order_sitetype)) #order locations

# Calculate max and dynamic breaks for the colors - calculates based on max relative abundance of dataset
max_abundance <- max(toplot2$relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)
alpha_breaks_raw <- max_abundance * c(0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00)
alpha_breaks_trans <- alpha_breaks_raw^(1 / x)


# heatmap 
asv_heatmap <- ggplot(toplot2, aes(x = site, y = taxa)) + 
  geom_tile(aes(alpha = (relative_abundance)^(1/x), fill = fill)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_colors) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(
    range = c(0, 1),
    breaks = alpha_breaks_trans,
    labels = scales::percent(alpha_breaks_raw, accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Sites (Mean Community)", 
    y = "Top 50 Genera",
    alpha = "Relative abundance (%)", 
    fill = fill) +
  theme(
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", face = "bold.italic", size = 9), 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", colour = "black"), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.background = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 1),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey95")) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(toplot2$taxa))

asv_heatmap
```

```{r}
library(shadowtext)

x <- 4  # nth root — keeps low-abundance cells visible when mapped to shading

toplot2 <- toplot %>% 
  mutate(
    site = factor(site, levels = order_sitetype),
    taxa = forcats::fct_relevel(taxa, "Unidentified", after = 0)  # Unidentified to bottom row
  )

max_abundance <- max(toplot2$relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)

# breaks evenly spaced in TRANSFORMED space, then back-transformed to raw values
# this keeps the legend labels from bunching up/overlapping
trans_breaks <- seq(0, max_abundance^(1/x), length.out = 6)[-1]
raw_breaks   <- trans_breaks^x

# heatmap 
asv_heatmap <- ggplot(toplot2, aes(x = site, y = taxa)) + 
  geom_tile(aes(fill = relative_abundance^(1/x)), colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_shadowtext(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", relative_abundance * 100)),
                   colour = "black", bg.colour = "white", bg.r = 0.15,
                   size = 2.3) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("white", "black"))(100),
    breaks  = raw_breaks^(1/x),
    labels  = sprintf("%.2f", raw_breaks * 100),
    name    = "Relative abundance"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Sites (Mean Community)", 
    y = "Top 50 Genera") +
  theme(
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", face = "bold.italic", size = 9), 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", colour = "black"), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.background = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 1),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey95")) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barheight = 12, barwidth = 0.8)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(toplot2$taxa))

asv_heatmap

```

## Core prevalence

```{r}
#Need to transpose first
asv_lakes_tss.t <- asv_lakes_tss %>% 
  t() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

asv_reefs_tss.t <- asv_reefs_tss %>% 
  t() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Calculate prevalence
# For lakes
prevalence_lakes <- asv_lakes_tss.t %>%
  select(all_of(core.lakes$ASV)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(. > 0))) %>% #gives the fraction of samples where the ASV is present
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "ASV", values_to = "Prevalence") %>%
  left_join(core.lakes, by = "ASV") %>%
  mutate(Habitat = "lake")

# For reefs
prevalence_reefs <- asv_reefs_tss.t %>%
  select(all_of(core.reefs$ASV)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(. > 0))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "ASV", values_to = "Prevalence") %>%
  left_join(core.reefs, by = "ASV") %>%
  mutate(Habitat = "reef")

# Combine both habitats
core_prevalence <- bind_rows(prevalence_lakes, prevalence_reefs)
```

## Barplot prevalence

```{r}
core_prevalence2 <- core_prevalence %>%
  # Replace NA with "Unknown"
  mutate(
    Phylum = ifelse(is.na(Phylum), "Unknown", Phylum),
    Genus = ifelse(is.na(Genus), "Unknown", Genus),
    Habitat = factor(Habitat, levels = c("lake", "reef"))
  ) %>%
  filter(Prevalence > 0) %>%
  # Order Phylum according to phylum_colors.core
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = names(phylum_colors.core))) %>%
  # Create helper column: reef prevalence per ASV
  group_by(ASV) %>%
  mutate(reef_prev = ifelse(Habitat == "reef", Prevalence, NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Arrange by Phylum and reef prevalence
  arrange(Phylum, desc(reef_prev)) %>%
  # Create x-axis ordering variable for ASVs
  mutate(order_var = factor(ASV, levels = unique(ASV)))

```

# Stats

## Community matrix

In order to use the package vegan and ggplot, we previously prepared the matrix "taxa_stacked" from the TSS transformation, and is now in long format. We need to set is as wide format, and with ASVs in columns in order to generate the community matrix for ordinations and permanova.

We generate one dataframe by ASV (OTU) and one by Phylum.

```{r}

#Data matrix based on ASV (OTU)
target <- "OTU"
columns <- c(unique(taxa_stacked$sample_id), target)
columns

# Filter taxa_info and remove rows with all zeros
community.asv <- taxa_info_all[, columns] %>%  #Selecting ASVs
  filter(rowSums(.[, -which(colnames(.) == target)]) != 0)

# Transpose and convert to data frame
community.asv <- t(community.asv[, -which(colnames(community.asv) == target)]) %>%
  as.data.frame()
community.matx <- as.matrix(community.asv) #convert to also have a matrix object to run ordinations
community.matx<- community.matx + 1e-6 #add pseudo count

#Final aggregated dataframe with sample ID
com.agg.asv <- community.asv
com.agg.asv$sample_id <- rownames(community.asv)

```

## nMDS variables

Saving variables to plot

scores(asv.nmds,display = "sites") #check scores/coordinates according to site and see if there are some data points where the range doesn't correspond with the rest.

```{r}
#Save the scores and merging with samples classifiers and variables
NMDS = data.frame(MDS1 = asv.nmds$points[,1], MDS2 = asv.nmds$points[,2])
NMDS$sample_id <- rownames(NMDS)
NMDS <- left_join(NMDS, env, by = "sample_id")

#Save scores of envfits
en_coord_cont <- as.data.frame(scores(envfit.asv, "vectors")) %>% 
  rownames_to_column(., var = "env.variables")
phy_coord_cont <- as.data.frame(scores(envfit.phyla, "vectors"))

# Save the ordiellipse function as an object
ordiplot(asv.nmds, type="point") #plot with ellipses
ordiellipse(asv.nmds, env$site, display = "sites", kind = "sd", conf = 0.95, label = T)
ord <- ordiellipse(asv.nmds, env$site, display = "sites", kind = "sd", conf = 0.95, label = T)

# Extract ordiellipse coordinates
df_ell <- data.frame()
for(g in levels(as.factor(NMDS$site))){
  df_ell <- rbind(df_ell, cbind(as.data.frame(with(NMDS[NMDS$site==g,],
                  vegan:::veganCovEllipse(cov = ord[[g]]$cov,
                                  center = ord[[g]]$center,
                                  scale = ord[[g]]$scale))), site=g))
}

#Save centroids and merge with NMDS dataframe
centroids <- aggregate(cbind(MDS1, MDS2) ~ site, data = NMDS, FUN = mean)
NMDS <- merge(NMDS, setNames(centroids, c('site','oNMDS1','oNMDS2')),
              by = 'site', sort = FALSE)

# Save each species score
species.scores <- as.data.frame(scores(asv.nmds, "species"))
species.scores$species <- rownames(species.scores)
```

## nMDS + envfit ggplot

Variables as factors for plotting. Adjust according to yours

```{r nmds variables}
plot.title <- "BCMs communities Raja Ampat - Level: ASV"
fill <- "Phylum"
env.variables <- c("connection", "temperature", "chla", "salinity")
# Define the variables you want to use for coloring
color_vars <- c("benthic_dom", "site_type", "site","influence_temp","influence_chla", "mat_color", "substrate_group")
```

Next, plotting the nMDS with the envfit vectors for the environmental variables.

The following is a loop where each plot is colored by different categories set in "color_vars". The plots are also saved in designated folder.

In the following chunk only adjust the export folder

```{r nmds ggplot loop}
for (color_var in color_vars) {
  
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = NMDS, 
               aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = .data[[color_var]],  # Use dynamic coloring
                   shape = site_type),    # Ensure site_type exists in NMDS
               alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
     geom_text(aes(label = sample_id), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 5) +
    
    # Control point size
    scale_size_continuous(limits = c(0.000001, 100), range = c(1, 10),
                          breaks = c(1, 10), name = "ASV \nMean Relative \nAbundance (%)") +
    
    # Use a colorblind-friendly palette
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "H") +  # or use scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2")
    
    # Customize shapes for the factors (optional)
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +  # Customize shapes as needed
    
    # Add labels and titles
    labs(subtitle = paste0("stress=", round(asv.nmds$stress, digits = 4)),
         title = paste0("NMDS Plot - Colored by ", color_var)) + 
    
    # Set theme options
    theme_bw() +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 14),
          plot.title = element_text(vjust = -6, size = 15, face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 12)) +
    
    # Add envfit vectors
    geom_segment(data = en_coord_cont, 
                 aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = NMDS1 *1.5, yend = NMDS2*1.5), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")), color = "black") +
    
    # Add labels to envfit vectors
    geom_text(data = en_coord_cont, 
              aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, label = env.variables), 
              color = "black", vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5)
  
  # Print the plots
  print(p)
  
  # Save the plots as pdf / change only directory
  ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/nmds/NMDS_plot_by_", color_var, ".pdf"), 
         plot = p, 
         device = cairo_pdf, width = 8, height = 6,
         units = "in", scale = 1, fallback_resolution=300)
  # Save the plots as png / change only directory
  ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/nmds/NMDS_plot_by_", color_var, ".png"), 
         plot = p, 
         device = png, width = 8, height = 6,
         units = "in", scale = 1, dpi=300)
  
} 

```



# PERMANOVA

Analysis of variance using distance matrices. Here we test the community against the environmental variables

Check this for complex models and how to write the formula: <https://uw.pressbooks.pub/appliedmultivariatestatistics/chapter/complex-models/>

[![Formulas for models. See ?formula](images_rmd/interactions.png){.illustration}]

```{r permanova and pairwise}
#PERMANOVAs
p.site <- adonis2(community_hell ~ site,
                  data = env,
                  permutations = 9999,
                  method = "bray", na.action = na.omit)
p.site

p.environment <- adonis2(community_hell ~ temperature * chla * salinity,
                  data = env,
                  permutations = 9999,
                  method = "bray", na.action = na.omit)
p.environment

p.categories <- adonis2(community_hell ~ mat_color + mat_substrate ,
                  data = env,
                  permutations = 9999,
                  method = "bray", na.action = na.omit)
p.categories

#Save permanova results in excel file 
p.sitedf <- as.data.frame(p.site)
write.xlsx(p.sitedf, path = "outputs/stats/p.sitedf.xlsx")
remove(p.sitedf)

p.envdf <- as.data.frame(p.environment)
write_xlsx(p.envdf, path = "outputs/stats/p.envdf.xlsx")
remove(p.envdf)

p.catdf <- as.data.frame(p.categories)
write_xlsx(p.catdf, path = "outputs/stats/p.catdf.xlsx")
remove(p.catdf)


#Pairwise analysis of significant variables
pw.site <- pairwise.adonis(community_hell, factors = env$site, 
                           p.adjust.m = "bonferroni", sim.method = "bray",
                           permutations = 9999)
pw.sitedf <- as.data.frame(pw.sitedf)
write_xlsx(pw.sitedf, path = "outputs/stats/pw.sitedf.xlsx")
remove(pw.sitedf)


```

# Indicator Species Analysis

To identify which species (ASVs) are indicators of specific groups. Here we test it according to site, influence, color.

Read more: <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/indicspecies/vignettes/IndicatorSpeciesAnalysis.html#data-required-for-indicator-species-analysis>

<https://jkzorz.github.io/2019/07/02/Indicator-species-analysis.html>

```{r function-IndVval.g}

## Using function IndVal.g
ind.origin.indvalg <-multipatt(community_hell, env$site_type,
                           func = "IndVal.g", control = how(nperm=9999))

ind.origin.indvalgdf <- as.data.frame(ind.origin.indvalg$sign)

# Extract significant species
ind.origin.indvalgdf <- ind.origin.indvalg$sign %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

# Create a dataframe for ggplot
ind.origin.indvalgdf$species <- rownames(ind.origin.indvalgdf) %>% 
  rename(.,OTU = X) %>% 
  select(-species) %>% 
   mutate(mat_origin = case_when(
    index == 1 ~ "bcm",
    index == 2 ~ "sed"))

# include taxonomy: comes from the taxa_info object
colnames(taxa_info)
taxa <- taxa_info[187:194]
colnames(taxa)

# Merge species indicator test with taxa

ind.origin.indvalgdf <- left_join(ind.origin.indvalgdf, taxa, by = "OTU")

#To save and not run the analysis again
write.csv(ind.origin.indvalgdf, file="outputs/indicatorsp_sitetype_bcm.csv")

```
